# The radius of an accumulator of one limb

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `acc_radius_1` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

Numbers of `T` that bound expressions of $a, m, g, t$ from above, valid when the mask $\mathit{ok}$ is true:

$$r \ge g (1 + u)^{2} (1 + m u + 2m^{2} u^{2}) (a + \frac{m \eta}{2}) + t.$$

## C++

No public operation computes this kernel on its own. It is part of [`acc_radius_2`](acc_radius_2.md).

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $a \ge 0$.
- $m = 0$ or $m \ge 1$, as a number of terms is.
- $g \ge 0$.
- $t \ge 0$.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- when $\mathit{ok}$ is true, $r \ge g (1 + u)^{2} (1 + m u + 2m^{2} u^{2}) (a + \frac{m \eta}{2}) + t$.
- when $\mathit{ok}$ is true, $m u \le \frac{1}{2}$.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `acc_radius_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/AccKernels.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/AccKernels.v), against `acc_radius_1_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions acc_radius_1_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition acc_radius_1_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (2 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall a m g t : R,
  fmt emin prec a ->
  fmt emin prec m ->
  fmt emin prec g ->
  fmt emin prec t ->
  0 <= a ->
  (m = 0 \/ 1 <= m) ->
  0 <= g ->
  0 <= t ->
  let '(r, ok) := acc_radius_1 emin prec tie_even a m g t in
  fmt emin prec r /\
  (ok = true -> ((((g * ((1 + u prec) ^ 2)) * ((1 + (m * u prec)) + ((2 * (m ^ 2)) * (u prec ^ 2)))) * (a + ((m * eta emin) / 2))) + t) <= r) /\
  (ok = true -> (m * u prec) <= (1 / 2)).
```

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `acc_radius_1_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the radius of an accumulator, in the form of conv_radius (milestone2.md); proposed here. **License:** proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/acc_radius_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/acc_radius_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# The radius of an accumulator of one limb (milestone2.md, "The accumulator": acc.error_bound()),
# in the form of conv_radius ("The product of polynomials"): roundings to nearest of nonnegative
# values, then one product by (1+u)^8 that covers the seven before it, and a constant that covers
# what the one product that may underflow loses and keeps the radius normal. The page gives it no
# listing: this one was proposed and checked in exact arithmetic by
# experiments/milestone2/accumulator.py. acc_radius_2 is the same listing: the magnitudes are summed
# in T for both numbers of limbs, and only (g, t) = bound_dot_k(m) differ.
#
# a is the running sum of the magnitudes of the leading limbs of what was added, m the count of terms
# (0 or at least 1), and (g, t) = bound_dot_k(m). The radius rests on the inequality of the page,
#   sum_i |x_i y_i| <= (1+u)^(m+2) (a + m eta/2),
# with (1+u)^m <= 1 + m u (1 + 2 m u) when m u <= 1/2 (pow_minus_1_le_gamma and gamma_le_poly of
# proofs/theories/Summation.v with eps = u): then g sum_i |x_i y_i| + t, the bound of dot for m terms
# in any tree, is at most the value of the claim upper below, which r is at least when ok.
#   q >= m u: q = RN(m ((1+u) u + N)), and q >= N for m >= 1   d = 2 q, exactly
#   w = RN(q + 2 q^2) >= (q + 2 q^2) / (1+u)                     c = RN(m N + a) >= (a + m eta/2) / (1+u)
#   e = RN(c (1 + w)) >= c (1 + w) / (1+u)                       f = RN(e g) >= e g / (1+u) - eta/2
#   s = RN(f + t) >= (f + t) / (1+u)                             r = RN(s K + C) >= (s K + C) / (1+u)
# with K >= (1+u)^8 and C >= (1+u)^7 eta/2 + N: r >= (1+u)^2 g (1 + m u + 2 m^2 u^2)(a + m eta/2) + t.
#
# The mask ok is false when m u may exceed 1/2 (d = 2 q exactly, so d <= 1 is q <= 1/2, written with
# the constant 1 of bound_dot_1 rather than a constant 1/2 that only a kernel without a real-model
# statement has, whose definition in IeeeModel.v would then change), and when a is not finite: a
# sum of magnitudes that
# overflowed (acc_add_k, acc_mul_k, acc_merge_k claim nothing of b where it is +inf), from which no
# radius may be believed. z = a - a is +0 for every finite a and a NaN for +inf and for a NaN, so
# eq(z, z) is the test that a is finite, written without the constant inf, which the real model
# does not have; in the real model it is always true.

q  = prod(m, const up((1+u)*u+eta/(2*u)))
d  = prod(q, const up(2))
w  = fma(q, d, q)
c  = fma(m, const up(eta/(2*u)), a)
e  = fma(c, w, c)
f  = prod(e, g)
s  = add(f, t)
r  = fma(s, const up((1+u)^8), const up((1+u)^7*eta/2+eta/(2*u)))
oq = le(d, const up(1))
z  = sub(a, a)
fa = eq(z, z)
ok = and(oq, fa)
```

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: what is proved and what is not written yet there is in [What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values).
